title: Leica LUX 2.0 yayınlandı: iPhone 18 Pro desteği ve Steve McCurry görünümü geldi
summary: Leica'nın iPhone fotoğrafçılık uygulaması LUX 2.0, iPhone 18 Pro desteği, yenilenen galeri arayüzü ve Steve McCurry imzalı yeni renk görünümüyle güncellendi.
body:
Leica LUX 2.0, akıllı telefon fotoğrafçılığına fiziksel kamera deneyimi getirmeyi amaçlayan uygulamanın bugüne kadarki en kapsamlı güncellemesi olarak yayınlandı. DIY Photography'nin aktardığına göre yeni sürüm, **iPhone 18 Pro** ve iPhone 18 Pro Max modellerine tam destek sunarken arayüzde de önemli yenilikler getiriyor.

## Yeni galeri ve harici uygulama desteği

Güncellemeyle birlikte uygulama, Leica FOTOS'un galeri arayüzüne kavuştu. Bu yenilik sayesinde kullanıcılar detay görünümünden doğrudan tekil fotoğraflar seçebiliyor veya ızgara görünümünde toplu seçim yapabiliyor. Ayrıca Adobe Lightroom, Capture One ve Darkroom gibi harici düzenleme uygulamalarına doğrudan erişim imkânı eklendi. Arayüzün genelinde ise Leica kameralardan ilham alan simgeler ve Apple'ın Liquid Glass tasarım diline dayanan görsel unsurlar yer alıyor.

## Steve McCurry imzalı yeni renk görünümü

Uygulamanın fotoğraf odaklı en büyük yeniliği ise fotoğrafçı **Steve McCurry** ile birlikte geliştirilen yeni Artist Look oldu. Renk, ışık, özne ve kompozisyon ilişkisine odaklanan bu özel görünüm, doğrudan bir fotoğrafı taklit etmek yerine kullanıcılara yaratıcı bir başlangıç noktası sunuyor. Greg Williams'ın ardından serideki ikinci olan bu görünüm, Leica LUX PRO aboneliğinin yanı sıra Leica FOTOS aracılığıyla Leica Q3 ve Leica SL3 modellerinde de kullanılabiliyor.

**Neden önemli?** Leica'nın milyonlarca kez indirilen uygulaması LUX, sunduğu manuel kontrol seçenekleri ve lens simülasyonlarıyla kullanıcıların telefonlarıyla daha profesyonel ve markaya özgü bir çekim deneyimi yaşamasını hedefliyor.

source_texts.title: Leica Wants Your iPhone to Feel Like a Leica Camera
source_texts.summary: Leica LUX 2.0 brings the iPhone deeper into Leica's photography ecosystem with a redesigned gallery, external editing support, a Steve McCurry Artist Look and iPhone 18 Pro compatibility. The post Leica Wants Your iPhone to Feel Like a Leica Camera appeared first on DIY Photography .
source_texts.text:
Leica Wants Your iPhone to Feel Like a Leica Camera
Leica has spent years making cameras that photographers carry because they want a particular shooting experience. Now it is trying to recreate some of that feeling on a device most people already have in their pockets.
Leica LUX 2.0 is the biggest update yet to the company’s iPhone photography app, adding support for the iPhone 18 Pro series, a redesigned gallery and a new Artist Look developed with photographer Steve McCurry.
Leica LUX Gets a New Gallery
One of the biggest changes in Leica LUX 2.0 is not a new shooting mode but the way photographers manage their images.
The app now uses the same gallery interface as Leica FOTOS, the company’s app for connecting compatible Leica cameras to smartphones and tablets. A new filmstrip allows photographers to select individual images directly from the detail view, while grid view now supports selecting multiple images at once.
Leica is also adding direct access to external editing apps. Adobe Lightroom, Capture One, and Darkroom can now be launched from Leica LUX, making it easier to move images into a more familiar editing workflow.
The interface itself has also been redesigned, with new icons inspired by Leica cameras and some visual elements based on Apple’s Liquid Glass design language.
Steve McCurry Gets His Own Look
The more photography focused addition is an Artist Look developed with Steve McCurry.
McCurry is known for his documentary, portrait, travel and landscape photography, with color playing a prominent role in his work. Leica says the new Artist Look focuses on the relationship between color, light, subject and composition rather than trying to reproduce a specific photograph.
That distinction is important. The company describes the look as a starting point rather than an automatic recipe for making an image resemble McCurry’s work.
It is the second Artist Look in Leica’s series, following one created with photographer Greg Williams. The McCurry look is available through Leica LUX PRO and can also be used with the Leica Q3 and Leica SL3 through Leica FOTOS.
Built for the iPhone 18 Pro
Leica LUX 2.0 also arrives with support for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Leica says the app has been optimized for the photographic capabilities of the new phones.
Existing LUX features include simulations of Leica lenses alongside manual controls for focus, exposure, ISO, and white balance. Leica has also continued adding features since the app launched in 2024, including Perspective Control, halation effects and monochrome color filters.
Leica says LUX has been downloaded millions of times and is used by hundreds of thousands of photographers each month. That gives the company a substantial audience for an app that is increasingly designed to feel like part of the wider Leica ecosystem.
The interesting part is how far Leica takes that idea. An iPhone will still be an iPhone, but LUX gives photographers another way to control how they use it. And if Leica can make people forget they are shooting with a phone, that could be the app’s most interesting trick.
[Photos via Leica]
Alysa Gavilan
Alysa Gavilan has spent years exploring photography through photojournalism and street scenes. She enjoys working with both film and mirrorless cameras, and her fascination with the craft has grown over the decades. Inspired by Vivian Maier, she is drawn to capturing everyday moments that often go unnoticed.
